charts.title: Which way does prediction run between summer temperature and tree rings?
charts.takeaway: Temperature leads: the index is +1.21 (+0.87 to +1.59) on the high-pass data, against 0.213 for rings paired with far-away sites, and it flips to −0.89 when time is reversed.
charts.units: direction index (the mean over sites of how much better last summer's temperature predicts this year's ring than the ring predicts next summer's temperature, in z units; above 0 means temperature leads, below 0 means the ring leads)
charts.n: 161 sites in 77 two-degree blocks; median series length 89 years; 199 far-site pairings
charts.interval: 95% interval from a block bootstrap (resampling whole two-degree blocks of sites) over the 77 blocks
charts.baseline: Each ring paired with the summer temperature of a site at least 1,000 km away: 95th percentile 0.213 (high-pass) and 0.186 (first differences)
charts.threshold: Real index above the far-site pairing's 95th percentile with its interval above 0, set in advance: held on both filters (+1.21 and +1.11)
charts.planted: A planted ring-leads world reads below 0 on both filters and a planted temperature-leads world reads above 0, so the index can show either direction

axis.label: direction index (above 0: temperature leads; below 0: ring leads)

charts.title: Did the method pass its own checks on made-up worlds with a known answer?
charts.takeaway: No: 2 of the 5 binding checks failed, both on first differences. A planted ring-leads world was read the right way at 58.4% of sites against a bar of 60%, and a shared trend alone made rings appear to predict temperature at 11.7% of sites against a limit of 10%.
charts.units: each row is one rule fixed before the data were read; rates are the share of sites with p at or below 0.05 in that direction
charts.n: 161 sites per made-up world, five surrogate draws per site
charts.no_interval: Each row is one measured value against a fixed bar. Rows named interval top use the upper end of the 95% block-bootstrap interval.
charts.threshold: Every binding check had to pass for the direction reading to get standing; any failure triggers the kill condition (the rule, fixed in advance, that withdraws the claim)
charts.planted: These rows are the planted checks: worlds built from surrogate series with a known direction, no coupling, or a shared trend only

charts.title: At how many sites does one series predict the other?
charts.takeaway: Last summer's temperature predicts this year's ring at 39.8% of sites. Rings predict next summer at 6.8%, no more than the 7.8% seen in a made-up world with no coupling at all.
charts.units: detection rate: percent of sites where the prediction test gives p at or below 0.05, high-pass data; a test with nothing to find gives about 5%
charts.n: 161 sites; the no-coupling world uses five surrogate draws per site; 199 far-site pairings
charts.no_interval: The result file holds one rate per row, plus the 95th percentile of the far-site pairing rate, given in that row's note.
charts.baseline: No-coupling world: 7.8% in the ring-predicts-temperature direction. Far-site pairing: mean 4.3%, 95th percentile 6.2%
charts.threshold: Ring-predicts-temperature rate on real data at most 10%, set in advance: held, 6.8% (high-pass) and 6.2% (first differences)
charts.ruled_out: Rings predicting next summer's temperature at more than a tenth of sites. The method's own failed checks on first differences limit how much weight this carries.

charts.title: A warm summer goes with a wider ring that year and a narrower ring the next.
charts.takeaway: The typical site's ring responds +0.17 to the same summer's temperature and −0.13 to the previous summer's; the previous-summer response is positive at only 21.7% of sites.
charts.units: median over sites of the regression coefficient of ring width on summer temperature, both in standard deviations, high-pass data; above 0 means a warmer summer goes with a wider ring
charts.no_interval: The check's output file holds medians and shares of sites, with no interval.
charts.baseline: A coefficient of 0 means ring width does not move with that summer's temperature
charts.threshold: None. This check was run after the results were seen and was not in the locked plan, so it is exploratory.

axis.label: median coefficient (above 0: warmer summer, wider ring)
